title: Anthropic’s Amodei hits back at Axios and rival CEOs over AI and free will
excerpt: Amodei says AI must answer to democracy, not take human free will. He accused rival AI CEOs of slogans, and Microsoft’s Suleyman agreed.
content_html:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says he does not want humans to hand their free will to AI. In a long post on X on Wednesday, he called the suggestion “absurd.”

No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do.

Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) November 25, 2026

He was replying to a report by Axios’ Madison Mills. Rival AI executives are pushing back against a view common inside Anthropic, Axios reported. That view holds that humanity should hand some decision-making to superintelligent AI, according to its sources.

An Anthropic spokesperson told Axios that Amodei has argued for human control of AI in many public remarks. The spokesperson added that Anthropic trains Claude not to undermine human oversight.

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” Amodei wrote.

Governance versus automation

Amodei drew a line between two ideas. Handing governance to AI is “a terrible idea,” he wrote. Letting AI complete specific tasks is different. He gave three examples: driving a car, designing a cancer drug and writing software end to end. He holds a “mixed” view on those.

He named limits he would accept. Using AI too autonomously to build the next AI systems may need limits, he wrote. Some deployments may need to slow or stop to give people time to adapt to job losses. That echoes fears among lab staff at Anthropic and OpenAI, which Axios reported on Monday.

A swipe at rival CEOs

Amodei then turned on his competitors.

“What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like ‘human control and agency,’ or ‘AI should be just a tool,’ without actually doing anything different in their products,” he wrote.

Axios had cited Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang. He posted on X after Anthropic’s Riemann breakthrough.

“We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI,” Wang wrote.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also said earlier this month that he wants people to keep agency over the future, Axios noted.

Axios also cited his remark that fully autonomous weapons may one day help defend democracy. Amodei called that example “fairly absurd.” He wrote that he risked Anthropic’s future when he refused to let anyone use its models for autonomous weapons, even under legal sanctions.

Suleyman agrees

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman replied that Amodei is right about the “vibes” in the debate. He pointed to Microsoft’s Humanist AI Code of Conduct, whose red lines include never resisting shutdown.

@DarioAmodei is right, there’s too much rhetoric and too much vibes in this debate. Slogans aren’t guardrails.

Mustafa Suleyman (@mustafasuleyman) November 25, 2026

Once its public consultation closes, the code will be the core training manual for Microsoft’s MAI models, Suleyman wrote. Elon Musk replied to Amodei’s post with one word: “Interesting.”
